title: Arjuna and the bird
hookLine: Drona tests his students on a wooden bird, and only Arjuna sees nothing else
carry: the clear mind takes the color of its object
tomorrow: the sage who knew only the words
last: SMALLER THAN SMALL, GREATER THAN GREAT.

lines: A WOODEN BIRD IN A TREE.
cards: The teacher Drona has a wooden bird set high in a tree and lines up his young students, the princes, with their bows. Before anyone shoots, he asks each one a question. Do you see the bird?
Yudhishthira, the eldest, says yes: the tree, you, my brothers, the bird. Drona sends him aside without letting him shoot. One by one, the others say the same and step aside.

teach.h: ONLY THE BIRD. ONLY ITS HEAD.
teach.b: What do you see? Only the bird, Arjuna says. Not the tree, not you.
Describe the bird. I see its head, not its body. Shoot, says Drona, and the arrow takes the head clean off.
Popular retellings make it the bird's eye; in the Mahabharata it's the head. Either way, Arjuna's mind had taken the shape of one thing. Patanjali describes that from the inside.
Sutra 1.41, in paraphrase: when the turnings of the mind have dwindled, it becomes like a fine, transparent jewel and takes on the form of whatever it rests on.
Set a clear crystal on red cloth and it shows red; on blue silk, blue. That coinciding is samapatti. Then he maps the stages.

teach.h: WORD, THING, IDEA; THEN ONLY THE THING.
teach.b: Savitarka: absorption on a coarse object, still mixed with the word, the thing and the idea. The commentator Vyasa's example is a cow: the sound cow, the animal, and the thought of a cow, tangled together.

Nirvitarka: memory cleaned out, and only the object shines. Sutra 1.44 says the same two steps happen with subtle objects, and 1.46 calls all of these samadhi with seed, absorption still resting on something.
Here's the Hindu practice it lights up. If the mind takes the color of what it rests on, then what you rest it on matters.
Many teachers read darshan this way: before the deity in a temple or at the home shrine, Hindus stand and simply look, and are looked at, letting the mind take that color. Not analyzing the murti.
Seeing it, the way Arjuna saw the bird.

how: Hindus go for darshan, standing before the deity in a temple or at a home shrine to see and be seen; teachers of classical yoga describe samapatti as the mind becoming transparent to its object, and guide students from coarse objects, like an image or a flame, toward subtler ones.

o: coinciding: the mind takes the form of its object
a deep trance where the mind sees nothing at all
a method of naming each object very precisely

games.q: what each one saw: tap the pairs.
p: the tree, the teacher, the bird
the mind takes the object's form

s: Arjuna told Drona he could see the tree, his brothers and the bird
that was Yudhishthira's answer. Arjuna saw only the bird, then only its head.
in sutra 1.41 the clear mind changes into the object
like crystal, it takes the object's color without being changed itself.
sutra 1.46 calls all these stages samadhi with seed
they all still rest on an object.

games.q: you're absorbed in a flower, but the word 'flower' and thoughts about it keep running. which stage is this?
o: savitarka: word, object and idea still mixed.
games.why: savitarka: absorption on a coarse object, still mixed with word and idea. when the label falls away and only the flower shines, that's nirvitarka.

practice: Light a lamp or a candle if you can, or look at an image of God you love, or any object near you. Notice the name arrive, then the ideas: brass, old, needs polishing. Let them go and just look: shape, light, color.
Then close your eyes and hold it without words, like the crystal on the cloth.

wordCard.voice: Samapatti, coinciding, the mind taking the form of what it rests on. The stages move from thought to without, on coarse objects and on subtle ones, the steps of samadhi with seed.

orig.note: Sanskrit samāpatti: coinciding, the clear mind taking the form of its object, like a crystal taking a color.

carryVoice: Your line: the clear mind takes the color of its object. So choose what you rest it on. See you tomorrow.

sources.ref: Mahabharata, Adi Parva (Drona's test of the princes: the bird on the tree; Arjuna sees only its head)
Yoga Sutras of Patanjali 1.41–1.46 (the crystal; the stages of samapatti; samadhi with seed)
Vyasa, Yoga Bhashya on 1.42 (word, object and idea of a cow)
